exec_summary: Site traffic (GA4, 2026-04-18 to 2026-04-24): growthbook.io had 11,026 sessions and 6,828 users (-8.3% week over week).

GrowthBook's organic search (GSC) grew to 3,633 clicks this week, up 6.5% from 3,411 last week, though impressions dipped from 123,585 to 106,901 -- worth watching but not alarming. The homepage alone drove 177 of those 222 net new clicks (branded search), so the underlying content-driven growth is more modest; the rest of the site contributed roughly 45 incremental clicks. GA4 session data was not available in this week's pipeline, so we can't speak to total traffic including paid and direct. Notably, GrowthBook published a significant wave of new content this week: a refreshed Experimentation product page, a Statsig migration guide, a Chess.com experimentation case study, and several blog posts covering AI A/B testing, experiment lift averages, fintech security, and vertical-specific roundups for healthcare and SaaS. These are too new to show GSC signal yet but represent a meaningful content push.

The single most important strategic finding this week is the deployment-related content gap that Flagsmith is exploiting across multiple high-intent topics -- deployment frequency, deployment strategies, and rolling vs. blue-green deployments -- all sitting at composite score 70. These queries sit at the intersection of feature flags and engineering workflow, exactly the audience GrowthBook needs to reach. Flagsmith owning this cluster means engineers evaluating feature flag tools may never encounter GrowthBook during their research phase. This is a direct top-of-funnel threat that warrants immediate content investment.

No new competitor pages were detected in this week's sitemap scan -- this almost certainly reflects a monitoring gap rather than all 10 competitors going quiet simultaneously. Unleash surfaces as a content gap threat on 'feature flags vs branching,' a topic directly relevant to GrowthBook's feature flag positioning. Comparison page performance was mixed: the GrowthBook vs. LaunchDarkly page dipped 3 clicks week over week to 5 clicks, and the vs. Statsig page dropped from 4 to 2 -- the newly published Statsig migration guide should help recover and grow that funnel over coming weeks.
content_recommendations: 1. Write a dedicated guide on 'feature flags vs branching' to close the gap where Unleash currently owns this query. Engineers actively evaluating branching vs. flag-based workflows are high-intent prospects for GrowthBook, and this topic has a composite score of 70 with no GrowthBook coverage today.

2. Expand into the deployment strategy cluster (deployment frequency, rolling deployment vs. blue-green, deployment strategies) that Flagsmith is targeting. These three related topics represent a coordinated Flagsmith content push into the feature flag evaluation journey -- GrowthBook needs at least one authoritative piece anchoring this cluster before Flagsmith consolidates authority.

3. Optimize for 'ab testing software' (position 8.89, 554 impressions) and 'a/b testing tools' (position 14.37, 547 impressions) -- both are striking-distance opportunities with high weekly impression volume. A focused on-page refresh of the most relevant landing page targeting these queries could push either into top-5, meaningfully increasing click volume.

4. Refresh the GrowthBook vs. LaunchDarkly comparison page, which slipped from 8 to 5 clicks this week and sits at position 8.1 with 1,042 impressions over 28 days. It is the highest-impression comparison page in the portfolio and a rank improvement to top 5 would be a significant traffic gain given query commercial intent.

5. Promote the newly published Statsig migration guide ('How to Migrate from Statsig to GrowthBook') through owned channels immediately. Statsig pricing changes have driven migration-intent searches, and getting early backlinks and social signals on this page will accelerate indexing and ranking before competitors fill this gap.
